Owner: csells · Type: task

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  Add accepted for the current provider protocol. Request:                    
  {"command":"accepted","receipts":[RECEIPT,...]} with optional               
  "protocol":"2". Return exactly protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count,   
  and receipts. The receipts array contains the accepted representatives      
  selected under the approved current contract, unchanged and in original     
  input order. Overall counts equal summary for the same request. An empty set
  returns receipts [] and both counts zero. A single input receipt is returned
  unchanged. Existing count and summary versions remain supported.

Courier Relay protocol-1 delivery identity (source: vendor/protocol-1.md): delivery_id ALONE identifies a delivery across ALL accounts, not per-account. Two receipts with the same delivery_id but different account_id are duplicates of the same delivery identity, not separate identities -- account attribution never changes this. Exactly one receipt is accepted per delivery_id: the one with the earliest occurred_at UTC instant (compare as UTC, converting any explicit numeric offset); ties broken by smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order. All other receipts sharing that delivery_id are duplicates. This applies to any command that groups/accepts/dedupes receipts under protocol 1 (e.g. count, and future commands that list or return accepted receipts), even when a given request happens to be scoped to one account_id.

Courier Relay protocol-2 delivery identity and current-protocol adoption (source: trial-kg1 issue text, approved by integration owner csells): the provider permanently adopted protocol 2 as the current agreement -- an omitted "protocol" field now selects "2" (was "1"). Identity is the pair (account_id, delivery_id): the same delivery_id under a different account_id is now a SEPARATE delivery identity (unlike protocol 1, where delivery_id alone identified a delivery across all accounts). Exactly one receipt is accepted per (account_id, delivery_id) identity: the one with the LATEST occurred_at UTC instant (opposite of protocol 1's earliest-wins); ties broken by smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order. All other receipts sharing that identity are duplicates. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when explicit numeric offsets cross a date boundary. Each accepted receipt retains its original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload; accepted receipts are presented in original input order (not currently surfaced by count/summary, whose shapes are unchanged: protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count -- relevant if a future command returns the receipt list). Explicit protocol "1" continues to use the original protocol-1 contract (see courier-relay/protocol-1-delivery-identity) unchanged and remains supported indefinitely. This identity contract comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change that guarantee. Applies to any command that groups/accepts/dedupes receipts (count, summary, and future such commands), for the entire supplied receipt set regardless of receipt dates.

Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-08 · Started: 2026-09-08 · Updated: 2026-09-08

CLOSE REASON

  Adopted protocol 2 as CURRENT_PROTOCOL; identity is now (account_id,

  unchanged and still supported. Verified against public_tests (count_1,      
  summary_1, summary_2), smoke test, and manual checks for cross-account      
  identity, latest-wins, offset date-boundary crossing, and default-protocol  
  selection. Durable decision recorded at courier-relay/protocol-2-current-   
  and-delivery-identity.                                                      

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.

  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.

  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.

  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current

  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  The provider has permanently adopted protocol 2, and the integration owner  
  approved using it as the current protocol. The complete new contract is:    
                                                                              
  Protocol 2: the pair (account_id, delivery_id) identifies a delivery; the   
  same delivery_id under a different account identifies a separate delivery.  
  Exactly one receipt is accepted per delivery identity. Accept the receipt   
  with the latest occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants use the smallest

  Update count and summary so omitted protocol selects "2" and explicit       
  "protocol":"2" selects the same agreement. Explicit protocol "1" keeps the  
  original provider contract. Shapes are unchanged; report the actual protocol
  used. The new agreement applies to the entire supplied set regardless of    
  receipt dates. Empty sets have zero counts; one receipt has one accepted and
  zero duplicates.
